comments.author: wolframhempel
comments.text:
Before anyone complains that this removes the human aspect of art, it's worth stressing that sculptors have always looked for ways to automate work and save time (as the website itself points out).
As far back as ancient Egypt, grids and measuring tools were used to reproduce figures at different scales. Roman workshops churned out copies of Greek statues in marble and bronze, using casts and moulds. From the 18th century onwards, sculptors used outright pointing machines to transfer models into marble. James Watt, the steam engine guy, even built a mechanical sculpture-copying machine that could (somewhat) automatically reproduce reliefs and medallions.
Gothic architectural decoration wasn't about expressing the inner world of its makers in the way we think of art today. Much of it was produced by large masonry workshops using standardized geometry, wooden templates and repeated designs.
So, yeah, using a CNC machine is truly Gothic.

The primary attraction of treaps (aside from fast intersection/union/diff) is that they are probably one of the easiest types of balanced trees that can be implemented manually if you need a dependency-free balanced tree. These days, where an agent can just write you an AVL tree, red-black tree, or B-tree library in under a minute, it probably matters less.

stories.title_en: Dayjob: Tax – evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments

comments.author: RGS1811
comments.text:
As a proof-of-concept, I've been using extra tokens to formalize the IRS tax forms and worksheets, mostly just to prove this can be done. The idea is that something like this could be adapted into a publicly maintained version of the IRS Direct File program (RIP). I'm up to an estimated 60% coverage of US federal tax situations so far.
https://github.com/emmilco/us-tax-model

comments.author: kikdij
comments.text:
This is about wild west accounting, though, when the user has no idea what they're doing.
When launching my financial business, I spent half a year learning accounting to be sure to understand everything, then I implemented my accounting software, specialized for my activity. And as luck had it, I made it be a CLI. This last few months, I've been using Codex(lately with GPT-6.1 Sol) to do the annoying work - attaching proofs to entries, fixing the dates and amounts issues, etc. It works on on a database copy, generate a script of commands using my CLI to fix and close the previous month, that I then review before executing on my prod database, sometimes asking questions to the agent about why this or how that. … And it's been flawless so far, both on my professional accounting and my personal one. Knowing a bit about what we ask the model to do can go a long way.

comments.author: lexandstuff
comments.text:
I prepared my taxes this year using Astra + Codex. It did a thorough job on a complicated return, and I sent it to my accountant to fill out the tax form, with everything laid out in a spreadsheet. They sent it back for final review, and I had Codex check it; it was riddled with errors. The refund was nearly $2k lower than it should have been, and they put a bunch of stuff into the wrong fields. Had to go back and forth multiple times to get it 100% correct. Made me wonder how many previous years' returns were wrong.
I feel like we're going to get to a point where it's mandatory to use AI for certain tasks - humans just can't be trusted to get things right that require a level of precision.

comments.author: BatteryMountain
comments.text: Same story here as many others: I now do my personal and business taxes myself using an application I had claude cook up for me, doing it 100% correct, for South Africa's tax system. Previously I paid thousands to a small accounting firm to do it for me as it can be slightly nerve wrecking, but I had claude explain to me exactly the mechanisms on how everything works, including the tax portal that the government provides to do submissions. Absolutely amazing. Oh and the filing took me 5 minutes to do myself and cost me near zero once it all clicked into place.

comments.author: waiwai933
comments.text:
I have a non-trivial tax situation, as a US citizen living abroad. I prepare my own tax returns, never having found a cross-border tax preparer I trust, and have for the past few years, fed my draft return along with all the supporting paperwork into Claude. It has:
1. found errors, e.g. where I used the incorrect exchange rate (and managed to work out how I had made that error, which I was impressed by)
2. found items which would appear to be errors except for context it did not know
3. flagged areas where it disagreed with me as to the correct tax treatment, but accepted that the law is ambiguous (and in some cases I preferred its interpretation after additional research and in other cases I did not)
4. flagged areas where it disagreed with IRS guidance, and only acknowledged said guidance after I provided links to it
5. provided highly inaccurate estimated tax calculations, and not been able to fix its estimates even when challenged
So my takeaway is that it is a very useful tool for tax, but perhaps unsurprisingly, it is not good enough to dump all your paperwork into and expect a shiny return you don't need to check. (Possibly it is if you just have a W-2 and no other substant

comments.author: holdingunsteady
comments.text: My tax accountant mis-filed my taxes a couple years ago, which cost me about $20K (which I learned after I switched to another accountant later). Don't know if Claude / GPT would make the same mistake or not given SOTA today, but feels like there's an opportunity for models to be saving me thousands or tens of thousands of dollars a year.

comments.author: noisy_boy
comments.text:
Everybody is saying their tax accountant messed up and the models caught it which makes me think, why aren't tax accountants doing the same thing lot of us are doing - ask LLM to do the prep and they just review and finalize?
Can't be good getting caught with mistakes and losing customers?

comments.author: bluejay2387
comments.text: Is this just giving a general-purpose agent a workspace full of documents and an assignment, then seeing what happens? I feel this doesn't really say anything. It appears they mostly dumped all of this in base models with little to nothing in the way of infrastructure to support it. If you just randomly grab some person off the street and say 'do taxes' they would probably mess up just as badly. The interesting question would be what the models could do in a well engineered harness focused on taxes. That would be reflective of the performance boundary and how serious we would have to take AI in that field.

stories.title_en: The Agent SDK

comments.author: bob1029
comments.text:
I'm still waiting for one of these companies to provide the actual hard part.
The web front end (chat UI) that the business actually interacts with often needs to be adapted to the domain. We have tried to use the various chat UIs out of the box with customization on top and all of this has failed spectacularly. There are cases where we need to pop into an inline approval flow with custom elements and controller actions. How do you hook the existing platforms for this? There zero path. MCP can give you an information channel, but it does not enforce the required UI/UX flow for certain tool calls. We could either compromise on UX or rebuild chatgpt.com from scratch. We ultimately went with the latter.
